basis: B-cell lymphoma defines blood and immune axes; splenic/marrow disease shares the blood axis. Liver infiltration is described, but a frequency of at least 30% is not established.

decisions.hepatic: none: increased liver involvement is not a quantified frequency; the supplied evidence does not establish involvement in at least 30%.

basis: Intellectual disability and developmental delay define disease. Skeletal abnormalities in 2/2 selected patients among a larger cohort do not establish a frequency of at least 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: scoliosis, camptodactyly and pes cavus each occur in only two reported patients; selected 2/2 denominators do not establish prevalence across the roughly 15-patient cohort.

basis: Respiratory ciliary dysfunction defines disease; chronic middle-ear disease with conductive hearing impairment affects over 50% in typical primary ciliary dyskinesia.

decisions.otologic: involved: impaired middle-ear clearance causes chronic effusions and conductive hearing impairment in over 50% of typical primary ciliary dyskinesia patients.

basis: Complex IV deficiency with defining cardiac and cerebral disease; retinopathy in 1/1 annotated patient supports ocular damage, with limited numbers. Hypotonia alone does not prove skeletal myopathy.

decisions.ocular: involved: retinopathy is direct retinal damage, reported in 1/1 annotated patient; accept provisionally given the very limited frequency evidence.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: the definition specifies encephalocardiomyopathy; hypotonia and spasticity can reflect CNS disease and do not establish common skeletal-muscle damage.

basis: Abdominal obesity/metabolic syndrome defines the metabolic axis; hypertension is explicitly annotated and is a major diagnostic component, rather than merely a later cardiovascular risk.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: hypertension is an explicitly annotated cardinal component of the metabolic syndrome phenotype and a major diagnostic criterion.

basis: Hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, hepatic injury and systemic microvascular endothelial injury define HELLP; glomerular injury with proteinuria occurs in 30-79%. AKI is rare.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: systemic endothelial injury and thrombotic microangiopathy define the syndrome; cardiovascular labeling does not depend solely on associated hypertension.
decisions.renal: involved: proteinuria in 30-79% reflects direct glomerular endothelial injury within the syndrome; rare severe AKI is not the basis for inclusion.

basis: Malignant neoplasm arising in hepatic blood-vessel endothelium; liver location and vascular origin are both defining.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: the tumor arises from hepatic vascular endothelium; blood vessels are explicitly covered by the cardiovascular axis.

basis: Microcephaly and intellectual disability define neurologic disease; macrotia is a named, defining external-ear structural abnormality. Hearing loss is not inferred.

decisions.otologic: primary: macrotia is a defining external-ear malformation named in the syndrome; primary structural involvement does not require demonstrated hearing loss.

basis: ID, hypogonadism and digital malformations define disease; ptosis/blepharophimosis occur in 30-79%. Sparse hair (80-99%) omitted at cap for functional eyelid abnormalities; hearing loss <30%.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis and blepharophimosis occur in 30-79% and affect eyelid function; prioritized over sparse hair at the four-axis cap.
decisions.dermatologic: none under cap: sparse hair occurs in 80-99%, but functional eyelid abnormalities carry greater organ impact; retain the defining neurologic, endocrine and skeletal axes.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: tapered fingers and short toes are in the disease definition; digital skeletal anomalies and toe contractures occur in 80-99%.

basis: LAT immune deficiency/dysregulation; autoimmune cytopenias directly affect blood in 2/3. Bronchiectasis/chronic lung disease (2/3) follows separate infections, so pulmonary is excluded.

decisions.pulmonary: none: bronchiectasis/chronic lung disease is reported in 2/3, but represents damage mediated by separate recurrent infections rather than direct pulmonary involvement by LAT deficiency.
